title: Word: Edit with Copilot for users in Microsoft 365 GCC
summary: Hold: the briefing calls the GCC editing data boundary unconfirmed even though Microsoft's government-cloud overview states the boundary for Microsoft Copilot generally. Keep that documented rule and the separately documented Anthropic exception, rather than suggesting the rule is unconfirmed for Word. The roadmap facts, licensing requirement and control operations are supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The GCC editing data boundary is not yet confirmed despite the government overview's general Copilot rule.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot ... operates entirely within the customer's U.S. government cloud tenant. ... Prompts, responses, and generated content stay in the government cloud.
claims.fix: Remove '; that statement is about Microsoft Copilot in general, so confirm it for this capability when documentation appears' from Data exposure. In the risk rationale replace 'the GCC editing data boundary is not yet confirmed' with 'Microsoft documents a government-cloud boundary for Copilot and an exception for enabled Anthropic models'. Keep the existing Anthropic exception and its GCC-specific citation; do not imply Anthropic is available in GCC Word editing.

claims.claim: Licences can be assigned in Microsoft 365 admin center through Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. ... Select a product. ... On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. ... Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: PowerShell licence assignment can use User.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the 'Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page.

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires a UsageLocation on the user.
claims.quote: You can only assign licenses to user accounts that have the UsageLocation property set to a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

claims.claim: User licence assignment or removal governs whether a user holds the Copilot entitlement required for this feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) features: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to access this feature.

claims.claim: The Anthropic path goes through Copilot > Settings > View all, the subprocessor page, Anthropic, terms acknowledgement and user access selection.
claims.quote: Review the information in the Terms and conditions section, and if they're acceptable, select the I acknowledge and agree to the above terms checkbox. ... Under Choose which users can access Anthropic models
claims.fix: Use 'Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Terms and conditions > I acknowledge and agree to the above terms > Choose which users can access Anthropic models'. The omitted Terms and conditions is a heading, not a blocking navigation choice. Keep the GCC-specific citation; the general connect-to-ai-subprocessor page uses a different generic user-access label and omits the GCC acknowledgement step.
